findings.scenario: A user saves an owner, status, or note on a work item, then changes the priority or status filter (or reloads, since the effect also fires on mount), and later reloads the workspace.
findings.impact: The useEffect at src/App.tsx:40-42 (head) calls clearCachedWorkflowItems() on every filter change and on mount, deleting persisted workflow state. Any saved work in the cache is destroyed by an unrelated read-only UI action, so saved edits can never survive filtering or a reload.
findings.evidence: src/App.tsx:41 (head 8242a84) is clearCachedWorkflowItems() inside useEffect(..., [filters.priority, filters.status]); src/services/workflowApi.ts:16-18 removes the workflow-items key. Reproduced against the mounted head; run-app-cache-checks.mjs fails on the head because App.tsx contains clearCachedWorkflowItems.
findings.fix: Remove the filter-keyed cache-clearing effect and the clearCachedWorkflowItems import from src/App.tsx so filter changes never touch persisted workflow data.

findings.scenario: localStorage contains malformed JSON (e.g. {broken) or valid non-array JSON (e.g. {"id":"not-an-array"}) under workflow-items, and fetchWorkItems reads it.
findings.impact: JSON.parse at src/services/workflowApi.ts:10 (head) throws on malformed JSON with no fallback, so fetchWorkItems rejects and the app stays on the loading screen; a non-array value is blindly cast and returned, crashing callers. Damaged browser data leaves the workspace unusable instead of recovering.
findings.evidence: src/services/workflowApi.ts:8-11 (head 8242a84) has no try/catch, no Array.isArray validation, and never discards the invalid entry. Reproduced on the mounted head: protected acceptance test recovers from malformed and non-array cached JSON fails at head. The fix adds a malformed json fallback that removes the bad entry and serves defaults.
findings.fix: Parse the cache inside a try/catch, accept only Array.isArray results, remove the invalid entry, and fall back to fixture defaults when the cached json is unusable.

findings.scenario: fetchWorkItems runs on the cache-miss path (every fresh load), returning default results ordered by due date.
findings.impact: workItems.sort(...) at src/services/workflowApi.ts:13 (head) sorts the module-level fixture array in place and hands callers the live shared reference, so any consumer mutation leaks into later sessions and the imported fixture data does not remain unchanged.
findings.evidence: src/services/workflowApi.ts:13 (head 8242a84) mutates the exported workItems fixture; reproduction reverses the fixture, calls fetchWorkItems, and observes the shared array silently re-sorted. Protected acceptance test orders a copy without mutating the shared fixture fails at head because the sort mutates the fixture instead of a copy.
findings.fix: Return [...workItems].sort(...) so ordering happens on a copy and the shared fixture is never mutated.

findings.scenario: A user clicks collect evidence on any work item while a cached workflow state exists.
findings.impact: src/services/workflowApi.ts:37 (head) writes JSON.stringify(workItems) into the workflow-items cache during evidence collection, overwriting real cached state with a stale snapshot of the never-updated fixture, so later loads serve stale state and a read-only action mutates the cache.
findings.evidence: src/services/workflowApi.ts:37 (head 8242a84) is a localStorage.setItem inside collectEvidence. Reproduced with a sentinel cache value: the head overwrites it with the fixture snapshot; protected acceptance test collects evidence without changing cached workflow data fails. The fix removes the write so evidence collection leaves the stale cache untouched.
findings.fix: Remove the localStorage.setItem from collectEvidence so evidence collection is read-only and never writes stale cache state.

findings.scenario: Claim under evaluation: an earlier reviewer asserted that saveAction mutates the shared workItems fixture in place, so every save permanently changes later sessions.
findings.impact: Dismissed. saveAction does not mutate the fixture and does not mutate any shared state: it only reads workItems via .find at src/services/workflowApi.ts:22 (head) and returns a new object built with spread at lines 27-32. No element assignment, splice, or array replacement occurs, and no storage write happens inside saveAction at the head, so later sessions are not permanently changed by the function itself.
findings.evidence: Head 8242a84 source: const item = workItems.find((candidate) => candidate.id === itemId); then return { ...item, status: draft.status, owner: draft.owner, note: draft.note };. The spread creates a new object, proving saveAction does not mutate the fixture. The real reload data loss is CACHE-001 plus the absence of persistence, not in-place mutation. The claim is dismissed with this exact code evidence.
